note: KID's own dependency layer. The engine's core is pure Node: everything it needs beyond the standard library appears here, with an identity, a licence and a hash. A hash mismatch is a failure, not a warning.
rules: the engine runs with zero UNLISTED dependencies
every entry declares kind, origin, licence, bytes and sha256 before it is used
a listed file whose hash differs is a failure until either the file is restored or the entry is updated deliberately
nothing is fetched at runtime: a dependency is obtained by an explicit, recorded step, never as a side effect

entries.name: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
entries.purpose: the MCP stdio server surface; the CLI and the core do not need it
entries.note: installed by the package manager from the declared range, so it is pinned by lockfile rather than by hash here

entries.name: kohane flac reader
entries.purpose: read FLAC metadata blocks and STREAMINFO and locate the first frame; decoding subframes to samples is the next stage
entries.note: verified against a real 150 MB master: 48 kHz, stereo, 24 bit, 30,543,355 samples, 636.32 s - matching the duration recorded independently | hash updated deliberately on 2026-10-15: the module gained its own capabilities declaration

entries.name: kohane matroska reader
entries.purpose: read Matroska/WebM container metadata: duration, timecode scale, and each track's type, codec id, video size and audio rate/channels/bit depth
entries.note: verified against a synthesised stream whose values were chosen in advance; elementary streams are not decoded

entries.name: kohane isobmff reader
entries.purpose: read MP4/MOV/M4A/3GP container metadata: movie timescale and duration, each track's handler, codec four-character code, pixel size and audio rate/channels
entries.note: verified against a synthesised file whose values were chosen in advance (3.000 s, avc1 1920x1080, mp4a 48 kHz stereo); samples are not decoded

entries.name: kohane ogg reader
entries.purpose: walk an Ogg page chain and identify what each logical stream carries (Vorbis, Opus, FLAC-in-Ogg, Theora, Skeleton, Speex) with its stated rate and channel count
entries.note: verified against a two-stream synthesised chain; packet payloads are located but not decoded, and page CRCs are not verified

entries.name: kohane riff reader
entries.purpose: read RIFF containers: AVI frame timing, size and per-stream headers, and WAVE format and data sizes
entries.note: verified against a synthesised AVI (1280x720, 25 fps, 250 frames, two streams) and WAVE (44.1 kHz stereo 16 bit, 1 s); AVI elementary streams are not decoded

entries.name: kohane flac writer
entries.purpose: write a FLAC stream: marker, STREAMINFO with the MD5 of the raw PCM, a Vorbis comment carrying the kohane vendor string, and frames with constant, verbatim or fixed-predictor subframes
entries.note: verified by round trip: the project's own reader reads the stream back, the declared MD5 equals the MD5 of the source PCM, and every decoded sample equals the source sample | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the independent bit-stream walk (tools/flac-walk.mjs) exposed three spec violations - subframe byte alignment that must not exist (RFC 9639 9.2: only the first subframe starts at a byte boundary), the tail-frame block size field now read after the frame number, and partition orders now required to divide the block size (RFC 9639 9.2.7); all fixed, and the walk plus ffmpeg both decode sample-exactly | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: escaped partitions (k=15) added per RFC 9639 9.2.7.1 - the 5-bit per-sample width field included - with a residual-range guard (a predictor whose residual leaves int16 is out, since every branch writes bps bits); a sine-plus-xorshift-noise fixture takes the escape path (escapes counted by the walk) and decodes sample-exactly through both the walk and ffmpeg | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: LPC subframes (orders 1-8) added per RFC 9639 9.2.3 - Levinson-Durbin with a quantisation search over precision 12-16 and shift -6..6, judged by the residuals the quantised coefficients actually produce. Three LD bugs were caught while a narrow-resonance AR(2) fixture failed to take the path: the recursion mixed the error-filter and prediction-coefficient sign conventions, updated coefficients in place reading overwritten values, and divided by a normalised-by-nothing energy. The fixture now takes the LPC path (lpc=22) and decodes sample-exactly through both the walk and ffmpeg

entries.name: kohane keygen synth
entries.purpose: generate audio from a score the keygen-music way: sine / square / saw / triangle oscillators with a per-note ADSR envelope, output as interleaved float PCM in -1..1 (mono)
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck synth section: the sine oscillator matches the analytic sine sample for sample, the square and saw shapes hold in sustain, release ends at a silent last frame with monotonically decaying window peaks, overlapping notes stay inside the unit range, the output survives the FLAC round trip through the independent walk, and a 61-byte score generates a 66194-byte WAV (1085x) - the volume argument keygen music rests on

entries.name: kohane soundfont reader
entries.purpose: read SoundFont 2 (.sf2) tables: preset names and numbers (phdr), instrument names (inst), sample names with rate and pitch (shdr), the preset and instrument bag/generator chains (pbag/ibag/pgen/igen - key ranges, velocity ranges, loop offsets, sample ids), the smpl data size and its offset - a whole font indexed without decoding a sample
entries.note: verified by a synthesised sfbk whose table values were chosen in advance, plus the real font D:/VSTPlugins/Soundfont Enhancer/Romantic Tp.sf2 (1 preset, 1 instrument, 146 samples, 44100 Hz) where present. The real font exposed the reader's first bug: the tables live after the sample data at the tail of the file, so a small probe window always missed them - the default now walks to the end | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the bag/generator chains joined the reader (preset and instrument zones with key/velocity ranges, loop offsets and sample ids) and the smpl chunk offset is recorded, so the bank conversion can extract sample PCM and enumerate key ranges and loops

entries.name: kohane FL preset reader
entries.purpose: read the indexable facts of FL preset and bank files (CcnK + FPCh/FBCh): plugin id, preset name, and the parameter body offset and size - what a preset library is searchable by, without interpreting any plugin's parameters
entries.note: verified by a synthesised FPCh/FBCh whose values were chosen in advance, plus real presets (Sylenth1 syl1, Darbuka WvpA) where present. The real files proved the name is a NUL-terminated string rather than the length-prefixed field the first guess assumed, and that .fxb banks carry FBCh where .fxp presets carry FPCh. The local index tool read 58406 files under D:/Sylenth1 into 7 plugin groups (58392 syl1 incl. 2212 banks, 8 XfsX, and single files from z3ta/SWSP/KLMV/Dune2), 1 unreadable

entries.name: kohane score, wave and view containers
entries.purpose: read and write kohane's own media containers - the .kbs score (title/tempo/key/parts/notes in the synth's second space), the .kbw wave envelope (min/max buckets over a declared frame count), the .kbv view layout (lanes, octave lines, palette) and the .kbm mix (tracks with gain/pan/route, buses, master, effect chains) - the '作编混' side of the .kb family, where third-party formats stay inputs
usedBy: lib/core.mjs (library_audio op=kbs, op=kbw, op=kbm and op=mix, and the kpb-install/kpb-verify media self-proof)
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck kpb media (stage 3) section: each container round-trips field for field, the score replays through the synth with the same frame count as a direct render, malformed scores are refused with the container's own name, the bundle self-proof passes all three checks on verify, a bundle whose score was emptied fails verification, and install refuses the same bundle | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the .kbm mix container joined the family (tracks with gain/pan/route, buses, master, effect chains), with read-time validation that every route names a declared bus

entries.name: kohane mixer
entries.purpose: render stems through a .kbm mix: per-stem gain and equal-power pan, bus routing with per-bus gain, master gain, and a strict rule that a declared but unexecutable effect refuses the render instead of being silently ignored
usedBy: lib/core.mjs (library_audio op=mix, the stems worker task)
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck kpb mix (stage 4) section: bus routing sums exactly (0.2 + 0.4x0.5 = 0.4), master gain closes the chain, the pan extremes isolate channels, a sine stem exported through op=mix equals the analytic sine x gain x the centre coefficient sample for sample, hard-panned stems isolate by channel, an unexecutable effect refuses the render, and the pooled render equals the one-core render

entries.name: kohane audio container
entries.purpose: store PCM in kohane's own container with a three-tier ladder: adpcm (IMA 4-bit, the default and the volume knob), lossless (delta through the built-in deflate) and raw (untouched int16); the header declares the tier so a reader never guesses
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck kpb assets (stage 5) section: the adpcm round-trip keeps the peak error inside 8% of full scale on a realistic spectrum and spans block boundaries, the lossless and raw tiers round-trip sample for sample, and the tier ladder shrinks for real (adpcm < lossless < raw) | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the encoder/decoder pair was rewritten to the standard IMA bit-by-bit form (the earlier quantisation split the code-7 branch between the two sides), and the raw-tier reader copies through the Buffer API so a pooled Buffer at an odd offset cannot break a typed-array view

entries.name: kohane instrument bank
entries.purpose: convert a SoundFont into kohane's own bank: every preset's zones enumerated with key and velocity ranges, root key and loop points, sample PCM deduplicated by content hash and stored as .kba (ADPCM by default, honest 2:1 low-pass decimation when the source rate allows) - the bank alone must enumerate instruments, key ranges and loops
usedBy: lib/core.mjs (library_audio op=kbb, and the kpb media self-proof for kbb)
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck kpb assets (stage 5) section: a zone-chain fixture converts to two zones with one deduplicated sample and enumerated key ranges and loops, the real Romantic Tp.sf2 converts inside the 8%-20% content-volume window, and a bundle carrying the bank self-proves it on verify | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the real font writes genCount 0 in its bags and leaves the count as the gap to the next bag's genIndex - the walker now takes the count when present and the gap otherwise, skips bags with no generators, and sample PCM is copied through the Buffer API so a pooled Buffer at an odd offset cannot break a typed-array view

entries.name: kohane single instrument
entries.purpose: carry one patch in kohane's own words: a name, a role in kohane's vocabulary (never a product name) and the byte-faithful parameter body, with a recipe field reserved for the day the parameters are written as a kohane synthesis recipe; converts FL FPCh presets and four-char-id binary presets (the FabFilter .ffp shape) in, one or in batch
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck kbi preset conversion section: FPCh and four-char-id conversions carry name, role and byte-faithful parameters, the document round-trips, foreign bytes are refused with the container's own name, batch mode walks a tree and reports the broken files, and the real Sylenth1 and FabFilter corpora convert where present

entries.name: kohane sample container reader (ztdw)
entries.purpose: read the custom sample container: the config (a note, then a deflated XML directory) enumerates every sample with its start, length, channels, bit depth, linear peak, pitch offset and round-robin number, and a merge file yields any region as PCM at the declared bit depth - the honest answer to the design's question whether PCM and key data can be extracted. The data base is probed (not guessed) and the receipts carry the declared peak, the observed peak and the gain ratio, because the stored samples are normalised
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck ztdw section: a synthesised config inflates to a populated directory with pitch and round-robin parsed, a merge region reads as 24-bit PCM with the declared peak observed, the op surface reports and extracts, and the real corpus (11 913 samples, 10 merge files) reads its recorded first entry at the probed data base with its recorded frames | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the real corpus exposed three format facts - the directory's length is a BYTE count (a frame count never lands on the next region's start), the data does not sit where the directory says (the base is probed by density, the first region living 192 512 bytes past its recorded start), and the stored samples are per-sample normalised with the declared maxPeakLin as the pre-normalisation gain (observed gain ratio 0.0308 against declared 0.03076)

entries.name: opna-render (external renderer, borrowed from 98fmplayer)
entries.origin: built from myon98/98fmplayer (BSD-2-Clause) - the freestanding libopna + fmdriver core compiled to a headless CLI by this project
entries.purpose: render PC-98 music files (PMD / FMP: .m .m2 and friends - the formats ZUN's PC-98 games used, plus .s98 streams) into a 55467 Hz stereo WAV through the OPNA (YM2608) emulation
entries.note: not shipped with KID: it is borrowed where it exists, looked up from KOHANE_OPNA first, then from this recorded path; when neither resolves, the engine says so instead of failing silently. The renderer was built at -O0 because the upstream core carries undefined behaviour that -O2 turns into silence, and with a narrow fopen because the wide open rendered silence on this MinGW CRT; sample output still varies between runs on this CRT (recorded in research/notes/2026-11-22-opna-98fmplayer-integration.md), so KID's checks assert the deterministic facts - exit codes, refusals and the WAV structure - while musical verification awaits real .m files

entries.name: kohane LM4 drumkit list reader
entries.purpose: read LM4 Mark II drumkit lists: the four-line header (kit name, sample folder, vendor) and every pad with its MIDI note, sample file, velocity layers, mute group and play mode - a kit is fully enumerable from its text alone, so the content indexes without touching the samples
entries.note: verified by the selfcheck lm4 section: a synthesised kit parses pad for pad (MIDI notes, velocity layers, mute groups, play modes), foreign text is refused with the kit's own header words, and the real converted kit on D:/LM4Mark2 reads with its full pad set while the content directory scans into kits and sample totals where present | hash updated deliberately on 2026-11-22: the mute-group and play-mode fields moved one position (they are the last two fields, positions 13 and 14 - the first guess read the two before them)

entries.name: ffmpeg (external decoder, borrowed)
entries.licence: as distributed by this build (the essentials build ships GPL components; confirm before redistributing)
entries.purpose: decode the compressed families KID does not implement itself (MPEG audio, AAC, Vorbis/Opus in practice, and the audio of video containers) into raw PCM
entries.note: not shipped with KID: it is borrowed where it exists and looked up from KOHANE_FFMPEG first, then from this recorded path; when neither resolves, the engine says so instead of failing silently

entries.name: kohane unity asset reader
entries.purpose: read a Unity scene, prefab, asset or .meta file: the document stream, class ids, object names, GUID references and the meta guid with its importer
entries.note: verified against a synthesised scene (ten documents, two guids, one prefab instance) and a synthesised .meta; the format is Unity's own documented YAML, not something recovered from a binary

planned.purpose: decode FLAC to samples, so op=pcm and op=play cover a lossless compressed family
planned.state: reader and writer both in place, with fixed predictors and Rice coding; higher orders, stereo decorrelation and finer partitioning remain
